title: Secure Cloud Operator - Lesson 7: Identifying AWS Account and S3 Buckets
objectives: Identify the AWS account ID associated with the current session.
List all available S3 buckets in the account.

mission_brief.situation: As a cloud security operator, you need to identify the AWS account associated with your current session and list all available S3 buckets.
mission_brief.mission: Use AWS CLI commands to retrieve the account ID and list S3 buckets.
mission_brief.execution: Execute the necessary AWS CLI commands to achieve the objectives.

content.walkthrough: Using the `aws sts get-caller-identity` command to retrieve the account ID and listing S3 buckets using `aws s3 ls`.
checkpoints: Verify the AWS account ID is correct
Confirm all available S3 buckets are listed

safety: Verify AWS account ID is correct before proceeding

bug_injection.bug: Incorrect AWS CLI command used to retrieve account ID.
bug_injection.fix: Use correct AWS CLI command `aws sts get-caller-identity`.

pass_conditions: Correct AWS account ID is retrieved
All available S3 buckets are listed
fail_conditions: Incorrect AWS account ID is retrieved
Not all S3 buckets are listed

interrogation_questions: What is the primary purpose of using `aws sts get-caller-identity`?
How do you ensure you are listing all available S3 buckets?

allowed: Using AWS CLI commands to retrieve account ID and list S3 buckets

resume_bullets: Securely identified the AWS account associated with my session
Listed all available S3 buckets in the account
